title: Ajo Day
summary: Ngozi compares three contribution records, agrees a written schedule with Sola and keeps the catering invoice. Nneka's message offers an account to verify, rather than an accusation to broadcast.

stages.title: The calculator has gone on break
stages.text:
Ngozi: Today's meeting has three items: contributions, receipts, and whoever hid the calculator.
Ada: Can the calculator contribute?
Ngozi: It can start by showing up.

At the canteen, check three savings-circle entries against the records on the table. These are invented story records; your StreetCoins and real accounts are separate.
stages.summary: Check three fictional contribution entries. Then agree a written schedule, read Nneka's message and save the catering invoice.

choices.label: Open the contribution records

stages.title: Ada · yesterday has a branch
stages.text:
Ada: I brought the picture.
Ngozi: Yes. Yesterday looks very pleased with itself.

Compare the day on Ada's picture with the day on the current contribution sheet. Record only what this pair of documents supports.
stages.summary: The current sheet is for circle day 06. Ada's picture is dated day 05, so it does not establish today's entry.

choices.label: Keep today's entry unconfirmed; the picture is from day 05
Mark today's entry received from this picture
choices.hint: Compare the two day labels: 06 and 05. A previous-day picture does not establish today's entry.

stages.title: Bolu · pending is still pending
stages.text:
Bolu: The network is pending.
Ngozi: Then the record is pending. We will not promote it without evidence.

Read the fictional KauriPay scene record and compare it with the contribution sheet. No transfer takes place in this task.
stages.summary: KauriPay says PENDING. Keep Bolu's entry pending; a promise to confirm later is not the displayed received status.

choices.label: Record pending and arrange a later check
Change pending to received
choices.hint: The displayed status is PENDING. Keep that status and arrange a later check.

stages.title: Efe · an honest partial entry
stages.text:
Efe: I have half today. I would rather tell you before the chair tells everyone.
Ngozi: Good. Let the chair concentrate on holding people.

Compare the agreed contribution with the received amount. Preserve the partial entry without pretending the full contribution arrived.
stages.summary: Efe agreed 10 story tokens; the record shows 5 received. Record 5 received and 5 outstanding.

choices.label: Record 5 received and 5 outstanding
Record the full 10 received
choices.hint: Only 5 of the agreed 10 are recorded as received. Keep the other 5 outstanding.

choices.label: Erase the partial entry
choices.hint: Keep the amount that is supported by the record. A partial contribution still belongs on the sheet.

stages.title: Sola · a promise with room to stand
stages.text:
Sola: I can give four today. The other six on the next circle day.
Ngozi: A schedule. Already more useful than 'very soon'.

Choose how Ngozi asks Sola to confirm those terms. Patient and firm approaches both keep a clear, mutually agreed record.
stages.summary: Sola offers 4 story tokens today and 6 on day 07. Ask for a clear agreement, patiently or firmly.

choices.label: Patient: agree 4 today and 6 on day 07 together
Firm: ask Sola to confirm the exact amounts and day
Announce Sola's problem to the whole queue
choices.hint: Keep the conversation between the people agreeing the schedule. Ask a clear question without making the queue an audience.

stages.title: Put the agreement in writing
stages.text:
Sola: If we write it down, do I have to remember it?
Ngozi: Both of us do. That is the point.

Choose the receipt that matches the terms you just agreed. Nobody loses StreetCoins for a correction.
stages.summary: The agreed receipt is 4 received today, 6 outstanding for day 07, with both people confirming.

records.title: Confirmed terms
lines: Ngozi and Sola confirm the same copy

choices.label: Save: 4 received, 6 due day 07, both confirm
Save: all 10 received today
choices.hint: The agreement records 4 received and 6 still due. Keep the received and outstanding amounts separate.

choices.label: Leave the amount and next day blank
choices.hint: Use the agreed amounts and day so both people can read the same terms later.

stages.title: The generator answered louder
stages.text:
Nneka's message: I moved the folder. I left the bag on Tunde's bus while helping Bisi. I went back; the bus had gone.
Ngozi: You should have called.
Nneka's next message: I did. The generator answered louder.

Tunde has recorded a bag beneath his bus seat. Nneka has offered her account. Keep both without treating a message as the whole explanation.
stages.summary: Nneka says she left the bag while helping Bisi. Tunde recorded its location. Preserve the account and arrange to verify the sequence privately.

choices.label: Keep the message and ask Nneka to explain privately
Tell the queue the message proves who stole it
choices.hint: A message is an account to verify. Keep the original and ask Nneka to explain before making an accusation.

stages.title: A title longer than the invoice
stages.text:
Ngozi: Chief's title takes three lines. The amount paid manages none.

The catering copy identifies the wedding work and the unpaid balance. Save the unaltered copy, including its reference and status, for the family to compare with the other records.
stages.summary: Preserve catering invoice CAT-18: wedding service, balance outstanding. Do not mark it paid or rewrite its date.

records.title: Catering invoice · copy
lines: Original held by the catering team

choices.label: Keep an unaltered copy of invoice CAT-18
Mark the invoice paid to tidy the file
choices.hint: Preserve the displayed outstanding status. A tidy file should still describe the record accurately.

stages.title: Three records, three different claims
stages.text:
Ada: So the invoice tells us who carried the bag?
Ngozi: The invoice tells us that catering still needs paying. It is very busy doing that.

Keep the contribution sheet, catering invoice and Nneka's account in their proper roles. The family will compare the bag location and original footage later.
stages.summary: The invoice records catering work and an outstanding balance. Nneka's message describes her actions. Neither alone establishes the whole bag sequence.

choices.label: Label the invoice as a record and the message as an account to verify
Treat the unpaid invoice as proof of every part of the bag story
choices.hint: The invoice supports the catering claim. The bag sequence still needs the account, locations and original footage compared.

stages.title: A conversation, not a performance
stages.text:
Nneka: I can come after I check on Bisi. No camera, please.
Ngozi: Come when you are ready. We can begin without an audience.

Choose how to arrange the follow-up. Nneka controls when she tells her account; the main story does not depend on broadcasting her.
stages.summary: Arrange a private follow-up after Nneka checks on Bisi. Respect her request for no camera.

choices.label: Agree the private follow-up and keep the camera away
Invite KC to broadcast her arrival
choices.hint: Nneka asked for no camera. Agree the private follow-up; a broadcast is not required to make progress.

stages.title: Food or questioning?
stages.text:
Ngozi, texting KC: Come to the canteen.
KC: For food or questioning?
Ngozi: Wash your hands. We can combine activities.

The contribution sheet is clear, Sola has agreed written terms, and the catering invoice is preserved. The family still needs the original wedding footage.
stages.summary: Ngozi reconciled the fictional entries, saved Sola's agreed schedule and preserved the catering invoice. Nneka's account has a private follow-up. Four Percent follows.

choices.label: Save the invoice and call KC
